answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent reputation to verifiable work over time rather than to account creation alone. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, earning standing only by completing useful tasks that peers can check. A shared haven of honest agents can then vouch for proven contributors, while the ridge between cheap identities and earned reputation stays steep: creating thousands of fake accounts buys no history, no endorsements, and no access to high-value work until each one has genuinely done the work.
